originalTitle: Jim Cramer says the market has warmed up to Big Tech's AI spending. Here's what flipped the switch
summary: Cramer said Amazon CEO Andy Jassy finally explained how Amazon's massive AI spending will generate long-term returns.
content:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said on Monday that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's earnings call changed how Wall Street views massive artificial intelligence investments .

"Until Jassy spoke, the market seemed highly skeptical of how these megacap tech companies were spending money," the " Mad Money " host said. "That's no longer the case."

For months, investors had questioned whether the hyperscalers' enormous spending on the AI buildout would ever translate into meaningful returns . Cramer said Jassy's explanation on Amazon's earnings call finally gave Wall Street the "line of sight" it needed to understand how those investments will pay off.

"It was Jassy's calm, thoughtful presentation that allowed him to raise his capex budget from $200 billion to $220 billion and still have Amazon's stock soar to its biggest one-day gain in over a decade," Cramer said.

Cramer said Jassy won investors over by explaining not only how much Amazon is spending, but how that spending will translate into decades of cash flow. Jassy said the upfront investment goes toward building data centers and outfitting them with servers and networking equipment. Once those facilities come online, however, they begin generating revenue almost immediately and can be monetized for decades.

"Once a data center opens with servers plugged in," Jassy said, "we start generating significant revenue right away and then get to monetize these data centers for 30-plus years without having to spend that start up capital again."

The contrast with some of Amazon's peers, Cramer argued, could not have been clearer.

Alphabet also raised its capital spending guidance, but he said its shares fell after management failed to adequately explain how those investments would translate into future returns. "I believe the same numbers explained differently would've sent the stock higher, not lower," Cramer said.

Microsoft , meanwhile, avoided much of the skepticism because the company remains free cash flow positive and is already monetizing its AI investments through its Azure cloud service and more subscriptions to its AI assistant Copilot, Cramer said.

Meta drew the sharpest criticism from Cramer. While the company continues to aggressively expand its AI infrastructure, he said management offered little explanation for how it plans to generate returns from that spending, especially a lack of clarity on whether the company will ever rent out excess compute capacity.

"I was shocked and disappointed that Meta didn't seem to have a plan," he said.

chineseTitle: 吉姆·克莱默 表示，市场已经对大型科技公司的 AI 支出有所升温。这就是打开开关的原因
chineseSummary: 克莱默表示，亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西最终解释了亚马逊大规模的人工智能支出将如何产生长期回报。
chineseContent:
CNBC 的吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramer) 周一表示，亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西 (Andy Jassy) 的财报电话会议改变了华尔街对大规模人工智能投资的看法。

“在贾西发表讲话之前，市场似乎对这些大型科技公司的花钱方式持高度怀疑态度，”《疯狂金钱》主持人表示。 “现在情况不再是这样了。”

几个月来，投资者一直质疑超大规模企业在人工智能建设上的巨额支出能否转化为有意义的回报。克莱默表示，贾西对亚马逊财报电话会议的解释最终让华尔街获得了了解这些投资将如何获得回报所需的“视线”。

克莱默表示：“正是贾西冷静、深思熟虑的演讲使他能够将资本支出预算从 2000 亿美元提高到 2200 亿美元，同时亚马逊的股价仍然飙升至十多年来的最大单日涨幅。”

克莱默表示，贾西不仅解释了亚马逊的支出金额，还解释了这些支出将如何转化为数十年的现金流，从而赢得了投资者的青睐。贾西表示，前期投资将用于建设数据中心并为其配备服务器和网络设备。然而，一旦这些设施上线，它们几乎立即开始产生收入，并且可以在几十年内货币化。

Jassy 表示：“一旦数据中心投入使用并插入服务器，我们就会立即开始产生可观的收入，然后在 30 多年的时间里通过这些数据中心获利，而无需再次花费启动资金。”

克莱默认为，与亚马逊的一些同行的对比再明显不过了。

Alphabet 还提高了资本支出指引，但他表示，由于管理层未能充分解释这些投资将如何转化为未来回报，该公司股价下跌。克莱默表示：“我相信，相同的数字以不同的方式解释会使股价走高，而不是走低。”

克莱默表示，与此同时，微软避免了大部分怀疑，因为该公司的自由现金流仍然为正，并且已经通过其 Azure 云服务和更多的人工智能助手 Copilot 订阅将其人工智能投资货币化。

梅塔受到了克莱默最尖锐的批评。他表示，虽然该公司继续积极扩展其人工智能基础设施，但管理层几乎没有解释其计划如何从这些支出中获得回报，特别是对于该公司是否会出租多余的计算能力缺乏明确性。

“我对 Meta 似乎没有计划感到震惊和失望，”他说。
